newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-HOCH GRABS SECOND ROUND LEAD AT SARAZAN WORLD OPEN.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-HOCH GRABS SECOND ROUND LEAD AT SARAZAN WORLD OPEN.

text.p: Scott Hoch fashioned one of the best rounds of his career on Friday to grab a two-stroke lead at the midway point of $1.9 million Sarazen World Open golf tournament on Friday.
Hoch carded nine birdies and just one bogey in his second round for a course record eight-under-par 64 at Chateau Elan.
He stood at 12-under 132 -- four strokes better than the previous halfway record in the short three-year history of the event.
Defending champion Frank Nobilo of New Zealand was second at 134 after a four-under 68. It was his eighth successive sub-par round here.
First round leader Todd Barranger was alone in third place, three strokes behind after shooting a 70.
"That has to rank as one of my best ball-striking rounds," said Hoch, who had one title this year and finished ninth on the PGA money list.
"It's the first time I can remember hitting every fairway and every green, especially on a quality course."
Hoch's lone bogey came at the first hole, where he three-putted after his approach shot stopped hard against the collar of the green.
"I wasn't close to being in the rough, and I hit a lot of good irons," he said. "On the four holes I bogeyed yesterday, I was three under today."
Nobilo stayed within striking distance of the lead with birdies at the final two holes.
"It was a hard working day because the course looked like it was there for the taking," he said.
Fifty-two players made the cut, which fell at three-over 147. Among the casualties was Scot Sam Torrance, who tied for second at last week's Volvo Masters, but struggled here with rounds of 73 76.
